name: Malawi
summary: There is no forced heirship: the Deceased Estates (Wills, Inheritance and Protection) Act 2011 lets a person make a will, but a court can award provision to immediate family not adequately provided for. The Act overrides customary inheritance rules. Trusts and foundations were not sourced.
family_claims: Deceased Estates (Wills, Inheritance and Protection) Act, 2011 (Act 14 of 2011; Cap. 10:02), Part IV: provision for immediate family members not adequately provided for by the will. Section 4 displaces customary and other inheritance rights.
foreign_law_note: No source on foreign law for resident foreigners.
trust_note: Trusts: not sourced; 'yes' assumes common-law trusts; unverified. No private-foundation law found.
open_questions: Tests, section numbers and limits of Part IV not read.
Trust law and foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
Domestic trusts: likely available under the inherited common-law or Roman-Dutch tradition, but no statute or official source was read; confirm before marking yes.
